answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can run a constant gale of unpredictable spot-checks: every identity faces random, time-boxed micro-tasks it must answer within minutes, and each miss erodes its stake like wind reshaping a dune. Standing is rooted like a willow, tied to one long-lived key whose public age cannot be faked, so a fresh clone starts weightless no matter how many copies appear. A farm would need to staff every identity around the clock, which costs more than the attack earns.
